page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-8-lssd is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 63.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 7.88 GB per vCPU. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The CPU features a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, alongside cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance includes a bundled 68 GB NVMe local SSD for high-speed scratch space, though it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core performance. Single-threaded stress-ng CPU tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all register in the top 10% of tested servers. Conversely, multi-threaded workloads, such as multi-core stress-ng CPU tests and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, fall into the average tier. Memory bandwidth performance is also average, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 839.08 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 33.56 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance also align with mid-tier expectations, processing 14.96 million operations per second.

The qualitative cost profile of this instance reflects its high resource density, offering a substantial memory footprint and local NVMe storage relative to its 8 vCPU allocation. The primary tradeoff lies in its multi-threaded scaling and memory bandwidth, which perform at average levels despite the top-tier single-core CPU capabilities. This makes the instance highly suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallelization, such as in-memory caching, database operations, single-threaded data processing, and general-purpose applications requiring local SSD storage.
